It captures technical insights, artistic critiques, procedural descriptions, and key event highlights relevant to CLO software users, 3D fashion designers, and digital garment creators. --- ## Event Overview and Structure This section outlines the event's agenda, introducing the hosts and describing the three-part structure of the live broadcast involving teacher reactions, annual review, and Q&A. - **Hosts Introduction**: Yana (community engagement via WeChat, Weibo, Douyin), Lili (10 years experience providing live broadcast info), Tina, and other participating teachers. - **Event Structure**: 1. Teachers’ reactions and evaluations of submitted student works. 2. Review of all 28 CLO live streams held during the year. 3. Q&A session addressing CLO software usage, teachers’ lives, and personal questions. --- ## Teachers’ Reactions to Student Works This section covers detailed critiques and feedback on selected student submissions, highlighting garment design, material realism, modeling techniques, and suggestions for improvement. ### Work 1: ID Lee You-sing - **Design Observations**: Dreamy aesthetic; loose bottom hem; perceived use of different colors. - **Critiques**: Top shirt appears thick; hemline folds deeper than expected; possibly "space cotton" fabric. - **Advice**: Authors encouraged to share construction details in comments. ### Work 2: Fan Tatika - **Visual Style**: Modern, magazine cover-like; black and white color scheme; dynamic with special effects. - **Details**: Texture clarity weak due to distance; stiffness in model's arm posture suggested for natural adjustment. ### Work 3: User YuEr - **Garment Details**: Red-themed work featuring wrinkle treatment; improved quality. - **Suggestions**: Add neckline details for realism; hat thickness could be increased; red smoke effect on back praised. ### Work 4: Kairin Wang (Bag Design) - **Craftsmanship**: Cotton material; voluminous bag structure; detailed zipper and buckle mechanics; zipper cover structure present. - **Feedback**: Floral pattern dense; zipper layers a bit stiff; overall high patience and skill required. ### Work 5: Chen Fuzheng (Hairpin Design) - **Features**: Hairpin with two small balls; possible couple’s outfit; distinct three-dimensional calligraphy effect on right side. - **Material Use**: Hair-dyed ball texture realistic; high-quality calligraphy. - **Suggestion**: Providing full-body match would enhance presentation. ### Work 6: Zhuang Zeyan (Multiple Outfits) - **Styles**: Dior-like elegance on left; high street style in middle; metal details on belt and shoes. - **Details**: Feather-like needlework textures; well-controlled fabric thickness; good attention to detail. - **Audience Interaction**: Fans eager for Q&A segment. ### Work 7: Kinsley’s Classmate (Hong Kong Student) - **Completed Set**: Hat, bag, jeans designed; some garments' hanging state unnatural. - **Learning Approach**: Student followed live classes closely; homework praised as exemplary. ### Work 8: Silence is the Best Choice (Two Works) - **Designs**: Contrasting styles with lace and bling bling jacket. - **Technical Notes**: Lace clarity low, especially at the bottom; suggestions include adding hair stickers/calligraphy or using CLO’s 6.0 metallic texture function.
